extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: A benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation, designed to bridge the gap in evaluating interactive visual artifacts generated by LLMs. ArtifactsBench comprises 1,825 executable queries across nine primary topics (e.g., Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications) and evaluates over 30 leading LLMs. The framework renders each artifact and captures its dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots, which are then assessed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge guided by a fine-grained, per-task checklist to ensure holistic and reproducible scoring.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.citeAs: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated via a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement. The process included: (1) Sourcing candidates from expert showcases, openSVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. (2) Automated filters to drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). (3) Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control using MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, and screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. (4) Prompt rewriting and difficulty calibration by experts and LLM rewriting for clarity/completeness/executability, with difficulty assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce a 30%/40%/30% split. (5) Checklist generation and calibration, where each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities, refined by humans for specificity and screenability. (6) Solvability validation and ambiguity repair by collecting candidate solutions from multiple families and pruning underspecified items. (7) Execution harness and screenshot policy using headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024×768 resolution with deterministic seeds, capturing three staged screenshots (before/during/after scripted interaction) to summarize interaction trajectories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: LLM Generation,Secondary Data analysis,Manual Human Curator,Software Collection,Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, openSVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, LLM visual-to-query from screenshots, and model-generated outputs evaluated against human preferences in WebDev Arena.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Automated filters were applied to drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control used MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, and screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Prompt rewriting and difficulty calibration were performed by experts and LLMs to ensure clarity, completeness, and executability.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset underwent de-duplication and contamination control using MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, and screenshot perceptual hashing. Prompt rewriting and difficulty calibration were performed by experts and LLMs to ensure clarity, completeness, and executability. Solvability validation and ambiguity repair involved collecting candidate solutions from multiple families and pruning underspecified items. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. The checklist is generated by Hunyuan-Turbo and human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration and achieves Cohen’s κ≥0.8 among annotators. The 10 items are grouped into five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions to support diagnostic analysis. The checklist is used to score the artifacts against task-specific criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Hunyuan-Turbo (for checklist generation), Playwright (for execution and screenshot capture), and Multimodal LLMs (Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B) as judges for scoring.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The MLLM-as-Judge scoring is validated via a 280-instance, six-model human study, demonstrating high pairwise agreement (targeting >90%). The analysis reveals systematic failure modes on intensive-interactive tasks and the insight that instruction-tuned generalist models often outperform specialist ones in this multimodal creative setting. The dual-referee setup (Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B) induces highly consistent partial-order constraints over model rankings, with residual differences concentrated among top systems.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbo (for checklist generation), Playwright (for execution and screenshot capture), and Multimodal LLMs (Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B) as judges for scoring.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is open-sourced, including the benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results. Versioning information and deprecation policies are not explicitly discussed, but the dataset is actively maintained and updated as part of the ArtifactsBench project.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No explicit mention of sensitive human attributes collected. The dataset focuses on executable artifacts and does not include personal data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to bridge the gap in evaluating interactive visual artifacts, which are central to user experience in modern applications. The framework emphasizes visual fidelity, interactive integrity, and holistic quality, addressing a critical bottleneck in the development of user-centric generative models. The social implications include advancing the development of models that better align with real-world user preferences and needs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases may arise from the sourcing of tasks from expert showcases, open datasets, and LLM-generated queries, which may not fully represent the diversity of real-world use cases. The difficulty calibration is based on aggregated performance of 30+ models, which may introduce bias toward certain model families or capabilities. The checklist generation and calibration process, while human-refined, may still reflect subjective judgments.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior by capturing and analyzing a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. The benchmark does not assess an LLM’s capability to function as an autonomous agent that can iteratively refine an artifact based on feedback or debug its own code. The dataset may not fully represent the diversity of real-world use cases, and the evaluation framework may not capture all aspects of interactive and dynamic qualities prioritized by human users.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine Tuning of LLMs for visual code generation. The benchmark is designed to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models by providing a scalable and accurate tool for evaluation. Usage guidelines include using the benchmark to assess the visual fidelity, interactive integrity, and holistic quality of LLM-generated artifacts.
